Azeroth Survivors tier list

Alpha disclaimer

This game is in active alpha. One balance patch can reshuffle any ranking below. Treat this as a snapshot of the current consensus, not a permanent truth. If you already have gear and talents on a character, staying on it is worth more than chasing a one-tier difference.

Class rankings by role

ClassRangeTierWhy
HunterRangedSSafe distance kills, free pet damage, strong single-target crits — best safety-to-power ratio for most players.
WarlockRangedSDoTs that corpse-hop, demon pets, self-healing — snowballs hard once talents come online.
WarriorMeleeSHuge health plus cleave, most forgiving melee; Whirlwind capstone turns into blender mode.
MageRangedAFastest screen-clear, three strong capstones — glass cannon with no pets to hide behind.
PaladinMeleeAEasiest first clear: Consecration, shields, self-heal, once-per-90s death save.
DruidHybridBFlexible kit, mid damage — viable with good talent luck.
RogueMeleeBBoss-melting burst but demands deliberate circling; punishes surround mistakes.
PriestRangedBSteady sustain, slower against dense waves.
ShamanHybridCChain Lightning scales with dense waves but ranks lowest in raw-damage breakdowns; most source-dependent class.

Sources disagree mid-table — one data-mined ranking puts Warlock/Warrior top and Hunter/Shaman bottom, while play-feel guides rank Hunter first. The safe read is Hunter, Warlock, Warrior and Mage as top picks; everything else depends on playstyle.

Pick for your goal

First clear → Warrior or Paladin. Forgiving positioning, self-sustain, death saves; learn the waves before the meta.

Power ceiling → Hunter or Warlock. Ranged safety plus scaling damage; Warlock especially snowballs with the right talents.

Highest burst, lowest tolerance → Mage or Rogue. For players who already know enemy movement.
